Look it up from the console

With tidystata loaded, findit() searches the same catalogue. Use a bare command, quote longer syntax, or supply variable names:

findit(reg)
findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)")
findit(tab, sex, region)

R functions and English or Chinese questions also work. Append |> print(n = Inf) to see all returned examples, notes and sources. See findit() for details.

Adapt an example

Replace illustrative variable names with yours. data is your dataset; data1 and data2 are merge inputs, and fit is a fitted model.

The R label names the main package. Load any packages needed for unqualified calls; many data-preparation examples use library(dplyr). findit() does not load or install packages.

About the notes

Differs from Stata flags a difference in defaults, missing-value handling, estimation or output; the note explains it. Other notes offer practical tips.

Execution checks test the R code, rather than numerical equivalence with Stata. Check missing values, weights, factor reference levels, join rules and standard errors before adapting an example. A search match does not imply support for every option.
